Terminal Fog

The fog takes the city apart and puts it back almost right.

The Repair People patch the city all day, one wall at a time. Some things cannot be patched. For those, Terminal City has the fog. Late at night, after the rooms have emptied and the Freight has taken away what cannot stay, fog comes in from the water and covers the shoreline, the tracks, the lights, the skyline, until enough of Vancouver is hidden for Terminal City to be rebuilt underneath. This is the full rebuild, the one that fixes what a brush cannot. When the fog lifts the city is back. Almost. One familiar thing is gone, or shifted, or slightly wrong, and nobody announces it.

After the Freight, the room host and a friend carry a folding chair through thinning night. At a familiar lane they disagree about which corner leads home; two drainpipes look much the same. From the closed garden gate comes the same short tapping phrase, over and over, though nobody is touching it. They put the chair down and wait. Fog softens the far wall. Rain crosses a shallow dry seam beside the raspberry roots, and the repeated phrase acquires one new beat. The familiar corner becomes legible again, with one masonry seam slightly displaced. A neighbour opens a door with a cup. The host taps the new beat on the chair before picking it up. By dawn a crow is examining the garden edge. Nobody announces that the whole city has been repaired.

The ruleEverything has returned so far.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
